title: Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State Relations (1988)
content: Comprehensive commission on federalism. Key recommendations: (1) Governor should be an eminent person from outside the state, not intimately connected with local politics, and appointed after consultation with the Chief Minister; (2) Article 356 should be used sparingly as a matter of last resort after exhausting all warning remedies; (3) Activate Inter-State Council under Art 263 as a permanent standing body; (4) Residuary powers of taxation should remain with Parliament, but other residuary powers transferred to Concurrent list.
high_yield_takeaway: The benchmark authority cited across UPSC GS2 Polity questions on Governor reforms and federal balance.

title: Punchhi Commission on Centre-State Relations (2010)
content: Updated review of Centre-State relations. Key recommendations: (1) Governor should have a fixed tenure of 5 years and removal should not be at the Centre's sweet will; removal should be through a process similar to the impeachment of the President by State Legislature; (2) Phasing out discretionary 'pleasure' doctrine; (3) Recommended localized emergency under Article 355 instead of bringing the entire state under Art 356; (4) Equal representation of States in Rajya Sabha.
high_yield_takeaway: Essential value-addition for modern UPSC questions on reforming the office of Governor and strengthening state autonomy.

title: Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) - Ethics in Governance
content: 2nd ARC 4th Report on Ethics in Governance. Key recommendations: (1) Creation of statutory National Ombudsman / Lokpal and Lokayuktas with independent investigation wings; (2) Comprehensive Whistleblower Protection Act; (3) Codification of civil service ethical values and code of conduct; (4) Fast-track corruption trials and reform of Article 311 disciplinary protection.
high_yield_takeaway: Compulsory citation for UPSC GS4 Ethics, anti-corruption mechanisms, and administrative reforms in GS2.

title: Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC) - Citizen-Centric Administration
content: 2nd ARC 12th Report on Citizen-Centric Administration. Key recommendations: (1) Institutionalization of the 'Sevottam Model' for service delivery excellence; (2) Making Citizens' Charters legally enforceable with compensatory remedies for service delays; (3) Mandatory Social Audits across welfare schemes; (4) Strengthening Right to Information (RTI) pro-active disclosure under Section 4.
high_yield_takeaway: Gold standard for public service delivery, good governance, grievance redressal, and accountability questions.

title: Law Commission 255th Report on Electoral Reforms (2015)
content: Key recommendations: (1) Disqualification of candidates upon framing of charges for heinous offenses rather than conviction; (2) Regulation of political party finances and transparency in corporate funding; (3) Legal prohibition of paid news and government-funded political advertisements during elections; (4) Strengthening independent regulatory oversight of ECI.
high_yield_takeaway: High-yield value-addition for electoral integrity, representation of people act, and democratic reforms.

title: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC / Venkatachaliah Commission, 2002)
content: Chaired by Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah. Recommended: (1) Inclusion of Right to Education as Art 21A (subsequently enacted); (2) Sensitization and implementation of Fundamental Duties (Justice Verma Committee); (3) Enactment of Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act; (4) Fixed parliamentary terms and constructive vote of no-confidence.
high_yield_takeaway: Widely cited for constitutional design, institutional checks and balances, and democratic deepening.
